title: Partition Array Such That Maximum Difference Is K
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find the minimum number of subsequences needed such that the difference between the maximum and minimum values in each subsequence is at most k.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find the minimum number of subsequences needed such that the difference between the maximum and minimum values in each subsequence is at most k. A subsequence is formed by removing zero or more elements from the original sequence while maintaining the order of the remaining elements.
constraints: Partition all elements into subsequences; because order within each chosen group is inherited, only its minimum and maximum values affect validity.
Return the minimum number of groups.
hints: Sort values so each optimal group can be represented as one consecutive sorted block.
Start a group at the smallest unassigned value and include everything no more than k above it.
Repeat from the next uncovered sorted value and count groups.
Any group containing the smallest remaining value cannot extend beyond smallest+k; taking every eligible value cannot hurt and leaves the fewest possible elements.
editorial: Any group containing the smallest remaining value cannot extend beyond smallest+k; taking every eligible value cannot hurt and leaves the fewest possible elements.

tests.explanation: Sorted values 1,2,3 form one group and 5,6 another, so two groups suffice.
With zero tolerance, every distinct value needs its own group, giving three.
